summary: The candidate fixes stale nonzero NCCL RAS gauges: normal registries remove recovered/disappeared labelsets and multiprocess registries zero them. It does not fully resolve the reviewed counterexample because multiprocess labelsets remain physically exported after recovery/disappearance, and the available AMD/RCCL single-GPU host cannot independently qualify the original NVIDIA NCCL 2.28.7+, two-node, or TP=2 runtime claims.

tests.what_was_measured: Original prepared base lacks the NCCL RAS module (ModuleNotFoundError).
Independently reproduced the stale nonzero AllReduce divergence after a recovered snapshot omitted that collective.
Candidate focused suite: 36 passed and 2 subtests passed.
Normal registry removes recovered collective labels and disappeared communicator labels, preserves the last snapshot across poll failure, and handles communicator reappearance.
Multiprocess mode retains the recovered AllReduce labelset; the candidate zeroes rather than removes it.

tests.command: at ac2aa3d: PYTHONPATH=/job/repo/python .../python -m compileall -q changed Python integration modules

gpu_execution.evidence: No qualified live NCCL RAS GPU execution was possible. Host has one AMD Instinct MI350X, Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2, and RCCL compatibility version 2.27.7.

remaining_counterexamples: With PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR set, nccl_ras_collective_divergence labelsets remain exported at zero after a recovered poll omits the collective.
With PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR set, per-communicator gauge labelsets remain exported at zero after the communicator disappears from a successful STATUS snapshot.
Live NVIDIA NCCL 2.28.7+ polling, two-node unresponsive/considered-dead transitions, and TP=2 serving metrics remain independently unverified.
remaining_limitations: The assigned architecture is AMD/RCCL rather than NVIDIA NCCL RAS 2.28.7+.
Only one GPU and one node are available; two-node liveness transitions and TP=2 serving cannot be reproduced.
No native source changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
